subject: history_social
passage: At Lothal, an Indus Valley Civilization site in Gujarat, India, archaeologists in the 1950s uncovered a large brick-lined basin more than 200 meters long. Because the town lay near a river that once connected to the sea, the excavators concluded that the basin was a dockyard where boats were loaded with goods for trade.
passage_b: Some archaeologists find the dockyard idea doubtful. They argue that the evidence linking the basin to boats is thin, and they note that ancient communities in dry regions often built large tanks to hold water. Archaeologist Meera Pillai suggests that the basin may instead have been a reservoir storing fresh water for the town, though she agrees that Lothal was an important center of trade.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the conclusion in Text 1?

choices.A: By arguing that the town of Lothal played no part in trade of any kind
choices.B: By agreeing that the basin was most likely used for loading boats with goods
choices.C: By claiming that the basin was built long after the town had been abandoned
choices.D: By proposing another use for the basin while accepting Lothal's role in trade

explanation.why: Text 1's excavators concluded that the basin was "a dockyard." Text 2 calls this idea "doubtful" and suggests the basin "may instead have been a reservoir," while Pillai "agrees that Lothal was an important center of trade." So Text 2 offers a different purpose for the basin without denying Lothal's trade.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Pillai "agrees that Lothal was an important center of trade."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 finds the dockyard idea "doubtful," so it does not agree.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 says nothing about when the basin was built.
explanation.D: Correct. Text 2 suggests the basin was a water reservoir but accepts that Lothal was a trading center.
